speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: asked	the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) what is Singapore's state of relations with China in view of the recent seizure of the SAF's Terrex Infantry Carrier Vehicles in Hong Kong; (b) how can Singapore continue to balance its existing trade and foreign relations interests with strong expectations from China to align with its One China policy and claims over the South China Sea; and (c) what are the Ministry's plans to normalise relations and minimise the impact of China putting more focus on competing economies in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As the Minister for Defence has already addressed the specific issue of the SAF's Terrex vehicles, I will focus my reply on the second and third part of the Member's question.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Singapore-China relationship is a long-standing, multifaceted and mutually beneficial one.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our top leaders meet regularly and there is a constant stream of official visits at all levels from both sides.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When Prime Minister Lee met Chinese President Xi Jinping in September last year on the sidelines of the G20 Leaders' Summit in Hangzhou, for which Singapore was invited by China, both our leaders agreed to strengthen our mutually beneficial relationship based on the principles of mutual respect and mutual understanding.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And over the years, we have built up a significant reservoir of trust and respect with our Chinese partners and stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In international relations, it is natural for countries to want other parties to act entirely in line with their own national interests.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As a small state, Singapore will, from time to time, encounter such expectations from other countries, and many of these other countries will be much bigger than Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However − and this is important − it is important for us to conduct our foreign policy as a sovereign, independent nation, and not be seen as acting at the behest of any other country.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is essential for our international credibility, standing, relevance and usefulness to our partners and friends.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must also maintain our emphasis on upholding international law and scrupulously respecting agreements which have been entered into with other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This attitude to international law and scrupulously respecting agreements is basic to the rules-based international order that benefits all countries and is especially crucial for our long-term survival and independence as a small state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have consistently abided by this policy and the understandings reached when we established diplomatic relations with China in 1990, and we will continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are not a party to the disputes in the South China Sea.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our position on the South China Sea has been articulated on many occasions, including by our Prime Minister, and our position reflects Singapore's need for peace and stability in our region, for freedom of navigation and overflight in major trade routes, and respect for international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore and the Chinese leaders and officials have continued to interact and we cooperate in many areas of mutual interest.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This partnership encompasses ASEAN, China, India, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We welcome China's growing engagement of our region as this creates new opportunities for mutual growth and prosperity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore's relations with China and our relations with other major powers should not be seen as a zero-sum game.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We believe in an interdependence characterised by an open, inclusive regional architecture that promotes collaboration and win-win outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If I were to be allowed to paraphrase President Xi, ideally, we should all be part of a common circle of friends.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But I think that for those who have followed the Chinese media, especially the state-linked media, they have also noted the discrepancy in what the government is doing and saying at the same time, versus what the media is also saying about Singapore and portraying Singapore to be.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, how do we handle this bi-dimensional approach that China is taking on its relationship with Singapore?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And is there any direct impact from our strained relations on market access of late?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, back to the Terrex comment earlier on, I know the Defence Minister covered this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given that MINDEF has mainly worked with the Hong Kong SAR government, and given our relations with China, and we know that there is a certain amount of influence that China has over Hong Kong, have we opened dialogue with the Chinese government to see whether we could mediate on this at the state level, between Singapore and China?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First, on the discourse which you hear in the media, we live in a new media age.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The tone of the discourse which you hear on private social media like WhatsApp versus public social media like Facebook, versus even the new media platforms of established government organisations or even state-owned enterprises, will differ in tone and will differ in the positions that are taken.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What I will say, on behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA), is that I do not believe in megaphone diplomacy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not believe in engaging in a whole lot of invective and in conducting affairs in a way which generates more heat than light.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, it is important that we maintain communications and engagement at the top level, similarly at the functional level, and also to continue interactions, businesses and people-to-people level.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, I want to encourage that these interactions on the business, commercial, cultural, educational and people-to-people levels should continue.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We should insulate these from issues that will come up from time to time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: However, if any association or any company has specific concerns, they can always approach me or the Ministry.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As far as I am concerned, and I have stated this before, we expect service providers providing services to the Government to comply with all local regulations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In this specific case, I expect APL to have complied with the local regulations.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is no need to engage in megaphone diplomacy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, let us have some patience and give this matter time to resolve through an appropriate legal or judicial process.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Would he agree that if the law is, in fact, being respected, the incident would not have happened in the first place?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The second supplementary question: I would like to ask the Minister what is his interpretation and assessment of a rising China and her behaviour, in relation to the detention of the Terrex vehicles.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, I would like to ask the Minister: has China's progress economically and militarily in becoming a superpower made her arrogant and aggressive and to become a big bully?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On the first question, I do not want to speculate.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Let the investigations be complete and let us see what conclusions Hong Kong arrives at.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is for the question on whether or not APL complied with the regulations that they were supposed to abide by.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not want to speculate or prejudge the issue.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second and third questions are really a broader issue, which is, that as China rises, as China gains both economic and military strength, what implications have that on us and the way they conduct international affairs and, indeed, on their relationships with the rest of the world?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I say this not in a facetious way, but I say this because we believe that a rising China, a strong China, one that is deeply engaged with the rest of the world and economically integrated is one that brings enormous benefits.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If we look at it from the historical point of view, never before in history have hundreds of millions of people been raised from abject poverty into an opportunity now where they can enjoy the prospect of being in the middle class and consuming at the middle class.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is an enormous achievement of China in the last 70 years.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If we look at the way Southeast Asia and even Singapore have progressed over the last 70 years since the end of the Second World War, there were several critical ingredients to this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: One is that we had peace and stability.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: These have been ingredients for us all to achieve progress and prosperity without war and conflict.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, looked against this light, we must welcome a rising China, a stronger China, an economically more integrated China.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we have to focus on the opportunities whilst at the same time recognising that there will be issues to resolve from time to time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is where we have to learn to take things in our stride.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are a multiracial society and we are located in the centre of Southeast Asia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What this means ‒ and I said it earlier ‒ is that, from time to time, other countries, big countries, will place expectations, quite frankly, sometimes, they will put pressure on us because they want us to completely align ourselves with their interests.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is where we, sometimes, from time to time, have to courteously, respectfully, differ and remind everyone, big or small, that please let Singapore be Singapore.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We may be small but we are an independent, sovereign nation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And if that means, from time to time, I have to have a difference with you, so be it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I am not against you; I am completely in support of your rise.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As to our attitude to international law, because of our circumstances and our Independence, the circumstances of our existence in the heart of Southeast Asia, international law and adherence to agreements are absolutely crucial to us.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a matter of the way Singapore got its Independence and the way Singapore will continue to remain an independent, viable nation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a ratio which I think no other country has.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And because of that, for us, trade is not a negotiating point; it is not a debating point.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, when we go round the world saying, "Look, we want to lower the barriers for trade because we believe this is a formula that has generated enormous opportunities and wealth for so many of us", that does not mean that free trade is an unalloyed good.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You have to be aware that for each nation that engages in this negotiation, you also have to ensure that you protect the vulnerable groups in our society.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Members of the House will also appreciate, in fact, that that is what we have been doing for the last 10 years.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we are trying to find that happy balance ‒ that happy balance between free trade and social security, between expanding opportunities and making sure no one gets left behind, between sometimes having to stand up to the big powers to tell them that we will have to have a polite disagreement, but we are still for you and we are not against you.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Do not force us to make invidious choices.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, that is really the strategic backdrop to the decisions that we make, the actions and the words we put.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope Members in this House and, in fact, I hope all Singaporeans will, therefore, understand.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Take this in our stride, remain calm, understand the big picture, do not panic.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like to say that I agree with his assertion of our country's sovereignty.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: But in the light of the comments made by China after the reports of the seizure and particularly comments that we should respect the One China policy and that they have communicated with us and that they have also requested that we abide by Hong Kong's laws, what are the grounds that the Ministry has to assume that China has not influenced Hong Kong's decision to detain the vehicles or in the decision-making process?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Minister share that with us and also.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: If that is the case, then why does the Minister consider those assumptions to be reasonable?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When I first got to MFA, the first lesson the diplomats told me was "assume nothing".

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I do not want to make any assumptions or presumptions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But having said that, I do not want to engage in conspiracy theories either.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I want to go on face value.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, this is the position which we welcome, and we await a resolution of this matter on that basis.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member has raised the other important point, which is on our One China policy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, because this is so important, I hope Members will bear with me if I repeat word-for-word what I said earlier.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have consistently abided by this policy and the understandings reached when we established diplomatic relations with China in 1990.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have always abided by it and I am standing here to state that we will continue to do so.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Some of the nuances of what I have said here may not be immediately obvious to everyone listening to this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But let me assure Members that the senior leadership in China, who are au fait with this issue, will understand exactly what I am referring to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I beg the indulgence of this House ‒ let us avoid politicising this and let us avoid megaphone diplomacy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Let us give this incident every opportunity to resolve itself in, I hope, an appropriate and sensible way.
